zap_no_target: No target is configured: set tools.<instance>.target to the base URL of a running local or disposable environment. Without a target ZAP cannot scan anything, so the stage is blocked, never passed.
zap_spec_missing: The OpenAPI specification {spec} named by the instance does not exist.
zap_auth_missing: The authentication of the instance reads the environment variable {env}, which is not set. Set it for the run; JGates never scans without the declared authentication.
zap_active_refused: The instance {tool} asks for an active scan, which sends attack payloads to the target and may change its data. It is refused unless the instance also sets allowActive: true (and the target is an environment you own and may damage).
zap_exit_error: The ZAP scan ended with code {code} (the scan did not run to the end): {detail}
zap_timeout: The ZAP scan exceeded the limit of {seconds} s; the step container was removed and the partial output kept in the logs.
zap_cancelled: The run was cancelled; the ZAP step container was removed and its partial output was kept in the logs.
zap_invalid_output: The ZAP report could not be interpreted: {detail}
zap_no_invocation: The plan has no ZAP invocation for the instance {tool}.
zap_condition_no_target: No target is configured: the stage is blocked until tools.<instance>.target is set.
zap_condition_passive: Passive mode: no attack payloads are sent.
zap_condition_active: ACTIVE mode, explicitly allowed by the instance (mode: active, allowActive: true).
zap_condition_risk: Alerts of risk {risk} or higher block.
zap_condition_auth: Authentication: the header {header} with the value of the environment variable {env} (never written in the plan).
zap_condition_image: Runs in the JGates tools image {image}, never pulled during the run.
zap_effect_requests: sends HTTP requests to the target
zap_effect_passive_spider: crawls the target from its base URL (spider) and inspects the responses with passive rules only
zap_effect_passive_api: imports the operations of the OpenAPI specification, requests them once and inspects the responses with passive rules only
zap_effect_attacks: sends attack payloads (injection, cross-site scripting, path traversal, command execution probes) to every reachable operation and parameter
zap_effect_data: may create, change or delete data in the target and trigger its security alerts
zap_effect_load: sends many requests for the length of the scan, which may slow the target down
zap_limitation_target: ZAP: runs only against the configured running target; passive by default, and the active scan only when the instance explicitly allows it; without a target the stage is blocked, never passed.
zap_setting_target: The target of the instance {tool} is {value}; use an http:// or https:// base URL without credentials, query or fragment.
zap_setting_spec: The spec of the instance {tool} is {value}; use a relative path inside the project.
zap_setting_mode: The mode of the instance {tool} is {value}; use passive or active.
zap_setting_allow_active: The allowActive of the instance {tool} is {value}; use true or false.
zap_setting_auth: The auth of the instance {tool} must be { header: <HTTP header name>, valueEnv: <environment variable name> }; the secret itself is never written in the configuration.
zap_setting_image: The instance {tool} names an image; ZAP runs in the JGates tools image and no other image can be used. Remove the image setting.
zap_setting_risk: The blockingRisk of the instance {tool} is {value}; use one of: {allowed}.
zap_setting_minutes: The spiderMinutes of the instance {tool} is {value}; use an integer from 1 to 60.
zap_fix: ZAP runs in the JGates tools image: start the container engine and download the tools of this JGates version (jgates setup), then run doctor again.
zap_form_target_help: Base URL of your application, already running (locally or in a disposable environment), for example http://localhost:8000. JGates does not start the application: start it before the validation. Never point it at production.
zap_form_mode_help: Passive only looks at the responses; active sends attacks.
zap_form_mode_passive_help: Crawls the application (or imports the OpenAPI) and only inspects the responses. It sends ordinary requests, no attacks.
zap_form_mode_active_help: Sends attack payloads (SQL injection, XSS...) that can change or delete the target's data and put load on it. Use it only on a disposable environment you own.
zap_form_allowActive: I understand: allow the active scan on this target
zap_form_allowActive_help: The active scan never runs because of the mode alone: this confirmation is saved as allowActive: true.
zap_form_spec_help: With a specification, ZAP imports the API instead of crawling pages. Leave it empty to crawl from the target URL.
zap_form_blockingRisk_help: Alerts at this risk or above make the check fail; lower ones are only reported.
zap_form_spiderMinutes_help: Maximum minutes the spider crawls the application (1 to 60).
zap_form_rule_active: To use the active scan, confirm that it may attack this target.
zap_form_capabilities_help: A profile turns checks on by capability: with this, the strict profile (or any profile with Runtime security) runs this ZAP instance.
